scope: Native source-closure fixtures compiled and run in a disposable ARM64 Linux VM with 1 CPU and 2 GiB. The real-clock quorum fixture runs nine loopback voter processes in three groups and uses the host wall clock; cell, admission and key input are synthetic. Other fixtures substitute time and quorum.
results: Numeric time refused before cell; valid synthetic live lease produced a receipt.
Synthetic expired, rogue and wrong-job requests refused before cell; lost or changed lease after cell suppressed receipt.
Synthetic backwards clock suppressed receipt; bypass mutant signed. Prior code signed expired and lost-lease cases.
Real wall clock and actual three-voter loopback quorum accepted live lease, refused expired lease before cell, and suppressed receipt after two voters were stopped during a delayed synthetic cell.
fault_injection: The synthetic cell explicitly flushes its in-flight marker via stderr before delay; two voters are stopped after that marker is observed.
limits: Voters share one VM and use unauthenticated loopback. Cell, key and admission are synthetic; fake clock is used for regression tests. No remote Mac, actual bot, authenticated independent quorum, wall-clock drift characterization, process-tree control, sink-side effect fencing or qualified governor. Suppressing a receipt cannot undo or fence effects. Do not blindly retry an unconfirmed outcome.
